punchline: He graded his own exams, then published where his grading was generous.
thirty_sec: Between October 2011 and September 2012 Scott Young worked through MIT's computer science curriculum from free course materials, sitting exams without notes and grading them against MIT's official answers. He admitted that a stricter recalculation would have put five finals below the passing line.
question: Which skill do you believe you have, but have never tested against a standard you did not set?
key_contrast: Feeling prepared versus a score you did not choose.
